idiom_name: kafka-go ReadBatch (ordered per-partition batch) with a header-keyed group buffer
implementation_notes: Go's messaging clients give ordered primitives but not the three-field protocol: Kafka orders messages inside a partition, so reading one partition with ReadBatch returns a contiguous, ordered Batch whose offsets already convey position, and NATS JetStream tracks a stream sequence with ordered consumers that reset when a gap appears. Numbering the parts of an oversized payload, detecting a gap and holding the group until the size or end marker arrives remains application code built on those primitives, so the classic header plus buffer-per-sequence form is the realization.
pitfalls: Kafka orders only within a partition: numbering a group that spans partitions (or that is re-partitioned when keys change) silently breaks the ordering assumption.
ReadBatch is bound to a single partition, so using it to drain a whole topic gives no global order.
Committing offsets automatically before the group is released loses parts permanently; commit only after a successful release.
